# Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Summarize whether BEAST2 is a valid alternative to RevBayes for the song evolution models, what changes when song types are modelled as stratigraphic ranges (sRanges), and the pros and cons of each option. The analyses and their details are in `source/revbayes_beast2_comparison.qmd`; this report reads its results from `output/pilot_5ms/comparison_summary.rds` and `output/pilot_5ms/ml/ml_estimates.csv`.

</div>

&nbsp;

# Load packages {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```{r load packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

sketchy::load_packages(packages = c("knitr", "ggplot2"))

theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 13))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dpi = 120, fig.retina = 1)

res <- readRDS("./output/pilot_5ms/comparison_summary.rds")
ml <- read.csv("./output/pilot_5ms/ml/ml_estimates.csv")
leks <- c("HC1", "BR1")

```

# Bottom line

- **BEAST2 reproduces RevBayes** under the same model (fossilized birth-death with sampled ancestors): the same parameters, the same trees, the same priors and the same clock model choice, in both leks and with both datasets
- **sRanges is a different model, not a different program**: it changes little in HC1, but in BR1 it changes the support of several clades of song types and raises the song loss rate almost three-fold. Since RevBayes and BEAST2 SA agree, the change comes from modelling song types as ranges
- **sRanges is not mature enough to rely on alone**: version 0.1.3, installed by hand, with fewer tree moves than SA (some flagged as pending review in its own example) and no way to check its fit to the data yet
- **Recommendation**: keep RevBayes for the main analyses, as in the first version, and use BEAST2 as an independent check. sRanges is worth considering as a sensitivity analysis, but only after testing its fit and its tree moves further

# What was compared

| Model | Software | How the first and last year of a song type are treated |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **RevBayes FBD** | RevBayes 1.4.2 (`dnFBDP`) | Two separate samples, with sampled ancestors |
| **BEAST2 SA** | BEAST 2.7.7, SA 2.1.1 | Two separate samples, with sampled ancestors |
| **BEAST2 sRanges** | BEAST 2.7.7, SRanges 0.1.3 | The two ends of one range (one lineage) |

All models share the substitution model (5-state GTR + gamma), the relaxed clock, the priors and the data: HC1 and BR1, MAFFT-optimal alignment, `new` records. RevBayes FBD and BEAST2 SA were run with the `bounds` (first and last year) and `all` datasets, and sRanges with `bounds`, the only one it can use. Each model was run twice. Marginal likelihoods of the global and relaxed clocks were estimated with 3 replicates in each program.

# BEAST2 and RevBayes

```{r similarity}

eq <- res$equivalence
eq_tr <- res$equivalence_trees
conv <- res$convergence
bf <- res$bf
bfw <- reshape(bf[, c("lek", "dataset", "program", "log_BF")], idvar = c("lek", "dataset"), timevar = "program", direction = "wide")

prior_note <- "Same distributions (HC1 bounds, sampled without data)"

similarity <- do.call(rbind, lapply(leks, function(l) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("bounds", "all"), function(ds) {
  m <- if (ds == "bounds") c("RevBayes FBD", "BEAST2 SA") else c("RevBayes FBD, all", "BEAST2 SA, all")
  b <- bfw[bfw$lek == l & bfw$dataset == ds, ]
  data.frame(lek = l, dataset = ds,
             largest_parameter_difference = sprintf("%.0f%%", max(abs(eq$difference[eq$lek == l & eq$dataset == ds]))),
             clade_support_correlation = eq_tr$correlation[eq_tr$lek == l & eq_tr$dataset == ds],
             largest_clade_difference = eq_tr$largest_difference[eq_tr$lek == l & eq_tr$dataset == ds],
             maximum_PSRF = max(conv$maximum_PSRF[conv$lek == l & conv$model %in% m]),
             log_BF_RevBayes = round(b$log_BF.RevBayes, 1), log_BF_BEAST2 = round(b$log_BF.BEAST2, 1))
}))))

similarity

```

Differences in parameter medians (origin, origination, loss and sampling rates, mean rate of change and gamma shape), correlation and largest difference in the support of clades of song types, convergence of the two runs of each model (PSRF, 1 means the runs agree), and log Bayes factor of the relaxed over the global clock.

- **Parameters and trees**: medians differ by at most `r round(max(abs(eq$difference)))`% and clade support by at most `r max(eq_tr$largest_difference)`. For clades, this is as small as the difference between two runs of the same program (up to `r max(ta_rep <- res$tree_agreement$largest_difference[grepl("1 vs .* 2$", res$tree_agreement$comparison)])`)
- **Priors**: sampling the model without data gives the same distributions in both programs
- **Clock model**: both favor the relaxed clock in all cases, and their Bayes factors differ by at most `r round(max(abs(bfw$log_BF.BEAST2 - bfw$log_BF.RevBayes)), 1)` log units
- **Two things to watch in BEAST2**:
    - The marginal likelihood printed by its path sampler (MODEL_SELECTION package) is 37 to 48 log units too low, so it has to be computed from the samples it saves, as done here (`source/pilot_5ms/ml/summarise_ml.R`)
    - The relaxed clock must use continuous rates with a prior: the default rate categories have no prior term, which does not change the posterior but inflates the marginal likelihood
- **Raw marginal likelihoods**: they agree in BR1, but in HC1 BEAST2 gives values 4 to 6 log units lower, because the two programs sample differently close to the prior. This cancels out when comparing models within a program

# Stratigraphic ranges (sRanges)

## What it changes

With sampled ancestors (RevBayes FBD and BEAST2 SA), the first and last year of a song type are two separate samples on the tree, and the first can be the direct ancestor of other song types. With stratigraphic ranges, both years mark the ends of a single lineage, and the years in between are integrated out. This is closer to what a song type is: one song that persists in the lek. As in the examples of the package, the sequence of a song type is placed at both ends of its range.

## Results

```{r sranges parameters}

res$shift[, c("lek", "parameter", "sRanges_vs_SA")]

```

Difference between the medians of sRanges and BEAST2 SA.

```{r sranges trees}

ta <- res$tree_agreement
sr <- ta[grepl("SA 1 vs BEAST2 sRanges 1|sRanges 1 vs BEAST2 sRanges 2", ta$comparison), ]
sr$comparison <- ifelse(grepl("SA 1 vs", sr$comparison), "SA vs sRanges", "sRanges replicates")
sr$clades_over_50pct_SA <- res$strong["SA", sr$lek]
sr$clades_over_50pct_sRanges <- res$strong["sRanges", sr$lek]
sr

s <- res$mean_support[["BR1"]]
s <- s[order(-apply(s, 1, max)), ]
data.frame(clade = rownames(s), round(s, 2), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)[1:8, ]

```

Agreement in clade support (correlation and largest difference) and number of clades with more than 50% support, followed by the most supported clades of song types in BR1.

- **HC1**: sRanges gives nearly the same trees as SA (correlation `r ta$correlation[ta$lek == "HC1" & grepl("SA 1 vs BEAST2 sRanges 1", ta$comparison)]`). Its parameters differ moderately, mostly a higher sampling rate
- **BR1**: the trees change. Support drops most for {`r res$top_loss`} (from `r round(s[res$top_loss, "BEAST2 SA"], 2)` to `r round(s[res$top_loss, "BEAST2 sRanges"], 2)`) and rises most for {`r res$top_gain`} (from `r round(s[res$top_gain, "BEAST2 SA"], 2)` to `r round(s[res$top_gain, "BEAST2 sRanges"], 2)`), and fewer clades are well supported. The song loss rate changes by `r res$shift$sRanges_vs_SA[res$shift$lek == "BR1" & res$shift$parameter == "Song loss rate"]` and the origination rate by `r res$shift$sRanges_vs_SA[res$shift$lek == "BR1" & res$shift$parameter == "Song origination rate"]`
- **Not a convergence problem**: the two sRanges runs agree with each other as closely as the SA runs do
- **Rates of song change are unaffected**: the mean rate of change and the gamma shape are similar in all models, so ranges affect the tree prior (origination, loss and sampling) more than the evolution of the sequences

BR1 has more song types recorded in more than one year than HC1, which may explain why ranges matter more there.

## Caveats

- **Tree moves**: sRanges has fewer tree moves than SA (no jumps between tips and sampled ancestors, no exchange moves), and its own example flags some of them as pending review. Agreement between replicates does not rule out that the moves affect the results
- **Maturity**: version 0.1.3, not listed in the BEAST2 package manager, so it was installed by hand
- **Fit not tested**: we have not compared the marginal likelihood of sRanges and SA, which would show which model the data favor
- **Only one dataset**: ranges can only use the first and last year (`bounds`), so they cannot be applied to the `all` dataset

# Run times

```{r run times}

rb_times <- read.csv("./output/pilot_5ms/run_times.csv")
rb_times <- rb_times[rb_times$exit_code == "0" & grepl("^(HC1|BR1)_5ms", rb_times$model), ]
bt_screen <- list.files("./output/pilot_5ms/beast2/screen", pattern = "^(HC1|BR1)_.*_10[12]\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)
bt_times <- sapply(bt_screen, function(f) as.numeric(sub(".*time: ([0-9.]+) seconds.*", "\\1", grep("Total calculation time", readLines(f), value = TRUE))))
ml_times <- read.csv("./output/pilot_5ms/ml/run_times.csv")

rng <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f to %.0f", min(x) / 60, max(x) / 60)
data.frame(analysis = c("MCMC (2 runs)", "MCMC (2 runs)", "Marginal likelihood (1 replicate)", "Marginal likelihood (1 replicate)"),
           program = c("RevBayes", "BEAST2", "RevBayes", "BEAST2"),
           cores = c(8, "1 per run", 8, 1),
           minutes = c(rng(rb_times$seconds), rng(bt_times),
                       rng(ml_times$seconds[ml_times$program == "revbayes"]), rng(ml_times$seconds[ml_times$program == "beast2"])))

```

Wall time for HC1 and BR1. Several runs shared the 32 cores of the machine, so these times are only indicative. In the MCMC, RevBayes runs 2 runs of 4 chains each in parallel, while BEAST2 runs 2 independent single-chain replicates.

# Pros and cons

| | RevBayes (FBD) | BEAST2 (SA) | BEAST2 (sRanges) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Results** | Reference | Same as RevBayes | Different trees and rates in BR1 |
| **Song types as persisting lineages** | No: two separate samples | No: two separate samples | **Yes**: one range per song type |
| **MCMC speed** | Slower (1 to 2 h with 8 cores) | **Faster** (20 to 45 min with 1 core) | **Faster** (similar to SA) |
| **Marginal likelihood** | **Built in and reliable** | Possible, but must be computed from the saved samples | Not tested |
| **Posterior predictive tests (P3)** | **Built in** (used in the first version) | Not available; would need our own simulation | Not available |
| **Maturity** | **Used in the first version, well documented** | **Well established** | Early version (0.1.3), installed by hand |
| **Tree moves** | **Full set** | **Full set** | Reduced, some pending review |
| **Datasets** | `all` and `bounds` | `all` and `bounds` | `bounds` only |
| **Setup** | **Existing scripts**; RevBayes 1.4.2 needs `dnFBDP` and an `age` column in the taxon file | XML files written from R | XML files written from R, more manual setup |
| **Collaboration** | **Familiar to the coauthors** (Beatriz runs it) | New to the project | New to the project |

# Options

1. **Stay with RevBayes (recommended)**: same design as the first version, with built-in marginal likelihoods and P3. Report BEAST2 SA as an independent validation on HC1 and BR1
2. **Add sRanges as a sensitivity analysis**: run it on the `bounds` datasets in BEAST2 and report whether treating song types as ranges changes the conclusions. Before this, compare the fit of sRanges and SA with marginal likelihoods, and check its tree moves (for example, by sampling from the prior and comparing with the expected distribution)
3. **Move everything to BEAST2**: faster, and it gives access to sRanges, but marginal likelihoods need our own estimator and P3 would have to be built and validated from scratch

# Still to test

- SUR, the lek with the most song types
- The global clock in the posterior comparisons, and the MAFFT-agnostic and PRANK alignments
- Marginal likelihood of sRanges vs SA
- Posterior predictive tests (P3) for BEAST2 runs
